symptoms: Small dark brown to black circular or angular spots on older lower leaves
Concentric rings develop inside spots creating a distinct target-board or bulls-eye pattern
Yellow halo (chlorosis) frequently surrounds older lesions; leaves dry up and droop
management: Prune or remove badly infected foliage where practical and dispose of away from production fields.
Irrigate at soil level (drip or furrow); avoid overhead sprinklers that cause prolonged leaf wetness.
Consult local agricultural extension for PCPB registered protective treatments during warm, humid weather.
prevention: Always source certified, disease-free seed tubers (from KALRO Tigoni, ADC Molo, or certified seed multipliers).
Practice minimum 3-year crop rotation away from potato, tomato, pepper, and eggplant.
Eliminate volunteer potato plants, cull piles, and nightshade family weeds.
Ensure balanced potassium and phosphorus to avoid plant stress.
monitoring: Scout lower canopy leaves every 3-5 days during alternating warm dry days and humid nights.
Track upward progression toward the upper canopy during tuber bulking.
escalation: Bulls-eye lesions advance rapidly from lower leaves into mid-canopy during tuber initiation.
Lesions spread to stems or tubers showing sunken dark lesions.
kenya_notes: Prevalent in major potato growing zones like Nyandarua (Ol Kalou, Kinangop), Nakuru (Mau Narok), Meru, and Bomet. Often secondary to nitrogen stress or drought stress.
